**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — no redline proposed.**

Section 14(a) of the General Provisions is the governing-law clause:

> "This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of Delaware... Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York, New York."

- **Governing law:** Delaware — expressly within the rule's fallback set (Delaware or California).
- **Forum:** exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York, New York — the preferred venue.
- **Arbitration seat:** Section 8 provides for AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules with no foreign seat, so there is no mandatory arbitration seated abroad and no walk-away trigger.

Two points noted in the rationale but not flagged as deviations: the law/venue mismatch (Delaware law applied by New York courts) versus the preferred all-New York package, and the internal tension between the Section 8 AAA arbitration mandate and the exclusive court jurisdiction in Section 14(a) — a drafting clean-up worth raising in negotiation rather than a playbook breach.
